title: Performance Playground: Compact model & route tiles with token-flow + cost overlays
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a compact, embeddable 'Performance Playground' tile set for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route performance signals (latency distribution, throughput bands, token flow waterfall, and token-level cost overlay). The Playground should be usable as a dashboard row, as a route detail panel, and as a lightweight inspector in DevTools. Key constraints: keep a compact footprint for lists, support expand-to-focus for microtraces, and provide a mode toggle between 'latency-first' and 'cost-first' views. Deliverables include high-fidelity prototypes, interaction specs, and chart rendering guidance for engineering (SVG vs WebGL tradeoffs).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Tile variants: list-compact (60–120px height), expanded (360px height), and full-page inspector exist in Figma with responsive behavior

A2: Charts: latency distribution (violin + pXX markers), throughput bands (area with request-rate overlay), token-flow waterfall (stacked timeline), and cost overlay (per-token shading) have pixel-specs and color tokens defined
A3: Interactions: hover shows microtrace snippet, clicking expands token waterfall to sequence view, toggle switches between latency and cost primary sort, and can pin a snapshot to a rollout variant

A4: Performance: recommendations documented for engineering (sample rates, pre-aggregation windows, fallback rendering modes), and a prototype demonstrates acceptable render with 200 concurrent tiles in the mock dataset
A5: Accessibility: all controls keyboard-focusable, color contrast meets WCAG AA for critical thresholds, and visual-only cues have text equivalents
A6: Hand-off: exported Figma file, a short PRD link, and a checklist for engineering QA included in attachments
comments: 2025-02-28 Aisha Patel: Initial pitch — inspired by user interviews where platform teams wanted a compact way to compare cost vs p95 latency across routes. Proposed 'Playground' as an embeddable row that can expand to a timeline inspector.

2025-03-01 Diego Rivera (Design review): Added initial layout options (left-aligned charts + right-side microtrace pane). Concern: token waterfall may be unreadable at list-compact size. Suggest progressive disclosure and a condensed token-sparkline for compact view.

2025-03-02 Priya Nair (PM): Prioritize rollout snapshot pinning for upcoming Dedicated launch. Request integration notes for rollouts so users can compare variant A/B performance in the same Playgrounds row.

2025-03-03 Mark Chen (Engineering): Reviewed chart rendering suggestions. Recommended WebGL for the token waterfall at expanded size but SVG fallback for list-compact. Flagged backend work: need pre-aggregated token buckets (ENG-5912) and microtrace sampling (ENG-6039).

2025-03-05 Design critique: team liked the 'cost-first' toggle but requested clearer SLO overlay patterns (dashed vs filled). Decision: use dashed lines for SLOs and a semi-transparent band for degraded region. Action: update component tokens and prototype.
2025-03-06 Diego Rivera: Updated Figma prototype link in attachments and captured interaction video. Ready for handoff pending engineering cost-of-render doc and security sign-off if needed.

design_decisions: D1: Use progressive disclosure for token-level detail: compact shows token sparkline, expanded shows stacked waterfall with token groups
D2: Color tokens: use the console palette with semantic mappings (good/ok/slow/failed) and a separate hue ramp for cost to avoid confusion
D3: Rendering: recommend WebGL for waterfall in expanded mode and canvas-accelerated area charts; SVG for list-compact and print/export
D4: Sampling: default microtrace sample rate 1% with UI control exposed to admins; pre-aggregated token buckets on 1min windows to keep payloads small
D5: Rollouts: snapshot pinning attaches metadata (model version, region, capacity tier) so Playgrounds can diff two variants side-by-side
